title: Senior Software Engineer Case Execution
description:
About Pivotal Health

Pivotal Health is the leading technology platform that helps healthcare providers get paid fairly in an increasingly complex reimbursement landscape.

Today, many providers face persistent underpayment from health insurance companies, despite delivering high-quality care. While processes like IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) were designed to promote fairness, theyâre often administrative-heavy, time-consuming, and difficult to navigate without the right tools.

Pivotal Health combines software, data, and service into a seamlessly integrated, AI-driven platform that simplifies these complex reimbursement workflows. We help providers efficiently dispute underpaid claims, reduce administrative burden, and recover the reimbursement theyâre entitled to; without adding more work to already stretched teams.

Our full-service IDR solution is just the starting point. Weâre building solutions that enable providers to operate with clarity, control, and confidence across the reimbursement journey.

About the Role

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer to join Pivotal's Case Execution team. This team owns critical parts of the case execution workflow, including eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These systems sit at the operational core of how Pivotal delivers outcomes for providers.

This is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys solving complex, workflow-driven backend problems and working through data-heavy decision logic. The most technically demanding areas for this team are eligibility and batching, and the right person is energized by that kind of work rather than looking to avoid it.

What You'll Do

  • Build and improve core case execution systems: Own backend development across eligibility, batching, submissions, ops workflows, and claim orchestration. These are the systems that determine how cases move through Pivotal's platform and reach resolution.

  • Tackle complex, data-driven backend problems: Work through the decision logic and data-heavy workflows that make eligibility and batching hard, understanding not just how individual systems work, but how they interact across the broader platform.

  • Contribute to workflow orchestration: Build and improve the systems that coordinate how cases are staged, routed, and executed end to end, with a clear eye toward correctness and reliability.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally: Work closely with the Integrations team, Case Strategy team, and other engineering and product partners to ensure systems are well-connected and aligned with how the broader platform operates.

  • Contribute to front-end and admin workflows where needed: The role is primarily backend-focused, but you'll contribute to internal-facing UI and ops tooling where the product requires it.

Who You Are

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience with a strong backend focus

  • Strong engineering fundamentals with hands-on experience building data-heavy, workflow-oriented systems

  • Experience working on complex, data-driven decision logic or orchestration problems: you're comfortable with systems where correctness and sequencing both matter

  • Comfortable operating in a collaborative, fast-moving startup environment where ownership and requirements evolve

  • Python experience; able to work effectively in a Python-based backend environment

  • Self-directed and proactive: you identify problems and drive them to resolution without heavy oversight

  • Strong communicator who collaborates well across engineering, product, and adjacent teams

Extra Credit If You Have

  • Experience with healthcare-specific data or HealthTech systems

  • Exposure to data-heavy architectures or problems adjacent to data engineering without being a pure data engineer

  • Familiarity with tools like Snowflake, dbt, or Databricks

  • Some front-end experience to support admin workflow contributions

Why Youâll Love Working Here

title: Head of Security
description:
Tremendous is the global platform built for businesses to send payoutsâgift cards and moneyâto anyone, anywhere, instantly. We're trusted by 20,000+ organizations, from startups to giants like Atlassian, MIT, and United Way, to reach millions of recipients worldwide.

We're profitable and growing without outside investors. We're fully remote, with a high-documentation, low-meeting culture that leaves more time for the work that mattersâand for your life outside it. Our employee NPS sits in the high 80s.

We move billions of dollars through our systems. That makes security existential, and it's why we're making our first dedicated security hire.

About The Role

You'll be our first Head of Security. There's already a real foundation hereâbug bounty, pen tests, automated code and configuration scanning on the production and code side, phishing simulations on the people side. Youâll add to it across access and identity, SecOps and monitoring, incident response, vendor security, employee security practices, and policy. You'll own the whole posture.

This is a player-coach role. Early on, you'll do the scoping and the hands-on work yourself; this is not a role where you direct from above. As the work demands it, we're fully prepared to build a team hereâand we're looking to you to define what that team should be and when.

You'll report to the VP of Engineering, Tremendous' most senior technical leader. We've deliberately placed security with Engineering so you're set up to drive real implementation fastâembedded with the people whose work you're securing, not siloed in a compliance function. As the security function matures, we'll revisit this.

What You'll Do

  • Own Tremendous' security posture end-to-end, partnering with our engineering team on production infrastructure and code security.
  • Assess where we have gaps, prioritize them, and tackle our highest-leverage gaps first. Weâll have opinions, but you own the prioritization and implementation.
  • Treat incident response as core, not afterthought. We may not be able to prevent a breach, but your job is making sure it's small, contained, and that we know exactly what to do.
  • Drive security as a cultural shift across the companyâintroducing controls incrementally, working with teams rather than over them. "Yes, and," not "no."
  • Lead our AI-security posture. We invest heavily in AI tooling; your job is to manage that risk and enable it, not to ban it.
  • Define when and how to staff up the security function, and hire your own team.

What You'll Bring

  • Real, hands-on security experience at a company that scaledâideally as an early security hire who grew with the business through high growth.
  • Deep experience in at least one core security domainâproduct/production security, security operations, or access/identity and policyâwith enough range to reason across the others. You defined the security posture, not just executed someone elseâs playbook.
  • An engineer's mindset. You reach for code to solve problems and can read our codebase and understand our infrastructure (Ruby on Rails; TypeScript + React; PostgreSQL; Google Cloud). You won't write much day-to-day, but you're not lost in the code.
  • Judgment over checklists. You can explain the actual risk of a given decision, hold a firm line where it matters, and give ground where "best practice" doesn't apply to us or real business need pulls the other way. You can hold your own in a debate about whether to open up broad data access for AI tooling.
  • Bedside manner. You drive hard change by bringing the team around to your point of view, rather than just telling them no. Engineers and the rest of the company want to work with you.
  • Experience building or co-building a small security team is a plus.
  • Fintech, payments, or regulated-industry experience is a plus.

What's Cool About The Role

  • You define the function. First security leader, with the budget for the required tools and team.
  • A real mandate. The push for this hire comes straight from the founders.
  • We invest in your tools. Everyone has a $5k/month budget for AI tools. Use it.
  • Competitive pay and equity. Base salary $250,000â$330,000, plus meaningful equity.
  • Fully remote. Work from anywhere in the Americas.
  • Great culture. Read more about how we work in our public handbook.

Compensation Range: $250K - $330K

Department: Support Operations

Reports To: Director, Support Operations

Location: Remote (U.S.)

Position Type: Full-Time, Exempt

Position Summary

The Clinical Coordinator Department Manager oversees the Clinical Coordination team responsible for maintaining accurate, appropriately filled provider schedules across all markets. This role provides leadership, operational oversight, training, workload management, process improvement, and cross-department collaboration to support consistent scheduling performance.

This leader sets daily and weekly priorities, delegates work, holds the team accountable, monitors current and upcoming schedule health, and identifies risks before they impact provider days. The manager ensures accepted treatment and unscheduled new-patient backlogs are actively worked and that scheduling barriers are tracked and escalated to the appropriate owner.

Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership & Performance Management

  • Lead, mentor, and develop Clinical Coordinators through clear priorities, delegation, accountability, and follow-through
  • Conduct regular 1:1s, performance reviews, coaching, and ongoing training refreshers
  • Oversee team scheduling, workload balancing, and coverage across markets based on provider days, appointment volume, and overall workload
  • Support onboarding and competency development for new team members
  • Foster a positive, efficient, and collaborative culture grounded in service excellence and ownership

Appointment Readiness & Schedule Reliability

  • Monitor the 0-14-day schedule and upcoming weeks to identify open capacity, underfilled provider days, and scheduling risks early
  • Ensure accepted treatment and unscheduled new-patient backlogs are actively worked in accordance with provider availability, market zoning, and scheduling priorities
  • Ensure Clinical Coordinators identify, track, and escalate scheduling barriers, including outstanding medical clearances, insurance verification, pre-medication needs, facility documentation, and lab-case concerns, to the appropriate department or owner
  • Monitor Clinical Days at Goal and schedule disruptions to ensure timely follow-up and improve filled provider days across applicable markets
  • Ensure schedules are entered timely and accurately while production-based scheduling remains focused appropriately

Root-Cause Analysis & Continuous Improvement

  • Analyze recurring scheduling barriers, backlog trends, fall-aparts, and schedule-health concerns to identify operational gaps and root causes
  • Develop preventive strategies and implement workflow or SOP improvements within Clinical Coordination
  • Coordinate any workflow change affecting another department or external partner with the appropriate department leader or Account Manager before implementation
  • Support system optimization, automation initiatives, and process refinements in CareStack and Healier

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner across departments to resolve scheduling barriers, maintain clear ownership, and support consistent patient flow
  • Serve as an escalation point for complex scheduling needs or facility and provider concerns
  • Independently address department concerns, communicate risks and updates, and escalate to the Director when additional leadership support is needed

Data, Reporting & Accountability

  • Monitor and report team performance and operational health indicators, including:
  • Clinical Days at Goal
  • 0-14-day schedule health and upcoming provider weeks
  • Accepted treatment and unscheduled new-patient backlog progress
  • Schedule-entry timeliness

title: Data Analyst Assistant
description:
About the role
 The Data Analyst Assistant role is central to our current engagement with a Dubai-based investment firm that requires precise data handling and clear visualization. This position provides the quantitative groundwork that allows our principals to form a view on complex corporate governance and strategy questions. We need an assistant who can organize messy data sets into logical structures that reveal the health and performance of a holding company.

About Arabian Private Holdings
 Arabian Private Holdings was founded on the principle that many critical business problems do not fit the traditional large-firm consulting model. A board facing a succession question or a family group weighing a capital injection does not need a team of twelve associates and a hundred-page methodology deck. They need experienced partners who can sit with a problem, form a rigorous view, and defend it. We take on a limited number of mandates to ensure that every client receives direct attention from the principals who are actually accountable for the outcome. Our work covers corporate strategy, governance, and operating model efficiency for some of the most significant family groups, listed corporations, and government entities in the region. We focus on clarity over complexity. We operate as a remote firm, choosing to prioritize the quality of our analysis and the strength of our relationships over traditional office overhead or aggressive growth targets.

What you will do
  • Collect and organize financial and operational data from various portfolio companies for a Dubai-based investment.
  • Clean and validate data sets to ensure accuracy before they are used in client presentations.
  • Build simple, effective spreadsheets that track performance indicators for large holding companies.
  • Assist in drafting reports that translate numbers into clear written arguments for our principals.
  • Monitor industry trends and perform basic market research to support ongoing strategic mandates.
  • Maintain internal records to ensure that historical client data is easily accessible and correctly categorized.
  • Prepare charts and graphs that simplify complex financial structures for board-level reviews.
  • Support the audit of corporate governance documents by cross-referencing quantitative findings with qualitative reports.


What we are looking for
  • A clear understanding of basic statistics and a logical approach to problem-solving.
  • Proficiency in spreadsheet software with an ability to manage large amounts of information without errors.
  • Strong written skills and the ability to explain what a set of numbers means in plain English.
  • Curiosity about how large corporations and family groups operate in different sectors.
  • Precision in your work, where you check your own calculations before submitting them for review.
  • A degree or ongoing studies in a quantitative field such as economics, finance, or mathematics.


How we work
 We operate as a fully remote firm, which means we rely on clear documentation and asynchronous communication. Because our work involves sensitive mandates for high-profile clients, we maintain a high standard of professional conduct and data security. You will work closely with a principal who provides direct mentorship and expects you to form your own view on the data you analyze. We do not value long hours for the sake of appearances. Instead, we focus on the rigor of the output and the clarity of the logic. This remote model allows us to hire individuals based on their intellectual capability rather than their physical location, ensuring we can provide the best possible advice to our clients.

What the role offers
  • A paid entry-level position with a competitive compensation package for the current market.
  • Direct exposure to high-level corporate strategy and governance mandates.
  • Mentorship from experienced principals who have managed some of the largest holding companies in the region.
  • The flexibility of a permanent, full-time role that is entirely remote.
  • Practical experience in forming a rigorous view on business performance and portfolio health.

description:
About Jimdo

We exist to unleash the power of the self-employed - helping solopreneurs and micro-businesses thrive by doing what they're passionate about and removing the complexity of building lasting, successful businesses.

Jimdo started in 2007 when three school friends built a website builder in a Northern German farmhouse to help everyone build a presence online. Today, we're a profitable, remote-first company with 220+ people from 50+ nationalities working across 15+ countries. We've helped build over 36 million websites to get online across the world.

We're more than just a website builder. We're an AI-powered platform that helps self-employed people actually run and build successful businesses — from getting found online, winning customers and running their business with a peace of mind by knowing exactly what to do next to move forward.

At the heart of Jimdo is a strong belief in personalized, data-driven guidance. Our platform combines design, business tools, and an AI-powered core that turns real customer data into clear insights and next steps helping our customers focus on what moves their business forward.

Role Overview:

Jimdo is becoming an AI-first company, and our People team is one of the first places where that shows up in daily work. We're looking for an AI & Data Analytics Partner to build the agents, analytics and workflow automations that make the People team faster, smarter and easier to scale.

You'll take a process from "this is slow and manual" to a working, compliant solution in production, and then make sure the team can run and extend it without you. You'll also give leadership one reliable view of People data, so decisions rest on numbers everyone trusts.

You’ll start with the People team, and the scope can grow to any other function across Jimdo.

The team and who you'll work with:

You'll report to the Manager Performance Intelligence and work day to day with the People team and our HR Business Partners.

You'll also work closely with our AI team on standards and capabilities, with Finance and Legal on data consistency and compliance, and with our HR system and payroll providers.

This is a remote role, open to candidates based in Germany, Italy, Spain or Portugal.

What you'll be doing:

  • Build a central reporting suite in Tableau that brings data from HiBob, payroll and compensation tools into one source of truth, with dashboards leadership actually uses.

  • Own the quality and structure of People data, and use analytics to spot workforce trends, risks and process bottlenecks.

  • Find the HR processes with the most friction and fix them with AI agents and workflow automation, from first prototype to production.

  • Improve self-service for employees and managers with AI tools that answer the repetitive questions, so the People team can focus on the work that needs a person.

  • Connect our systems of record and improve the data flow between HR and Finance, so there's far less manual reconciliation.

  • Make every solution auditable, explainable and compliant, and set clear guardrails for responsible AI use.

  • Run hands-on workshops and co-building sessions and write playbooks, so the team can build and maintain automations on their own.

Your first months:

  • After 3 months: you know our People systems and data flows, you've agreed the reporting scope with the People team, and your first quick-win automation is live.

  • After 6 months: the central reporting suite is in use by leadership, and at least one AI-enabled HR process runs in production

What you bring to the table:

  • 5+ years in data analytics, AI and automation, or technical systems roles.

  • 2+ years of hands-on work with LLMs, agents, prompt engineering and workflow orchestration tools such as n8n, with solutions you've taken into production.

  • A track record of improving business processes through automation or system redesign, with results you can show.

  • Strong data analysis skills and expert-level Tableau: you build dashboards that turn complex data into clear recommendations. Database knowledge is a plus.

  • Expert knowledge of HiBob as a user, including its data and reporting, and a solid sense of data privacy and compliance (GDPR) when handling sensitive people data.

  • You enjoy teaching: you explain technical choices in plain language and measure your success by how well others can use what you've built.

Nice to have

  • A certification in AI, machine learning, analytics or automation.

  • Experience working with Finance, Legal or external HR service providers.

What we offer:

Inspiring Mission: At our core, we are driven by a meaningful mission - to  empower solopreneurs and small businesses to succeed and  to contribute to the sustainability and vibrancy of the communities they serve.

Flexibility and Trust: Our work environment thrives on flexibility and trust. We offer fully remote work set-up  with opportunities for in-person collaboration. You can manage your working hours flexibly because we prioritize the results you deliver over the number of hours you put in. 

An International Diverse Team: Our team is a mosaic of over 248 individuals hailing from 50+ different countries and working across 15+ diverse locations. We take pride in our openness and inclusivity.

Continuous  Growth and Career Development: We invest in your growth with company-wide access to LinkedIn Learning and curated learning paths. From day one, you have the chance to contribute your ideas and create a meaningful impact. Our flat hierarchies and swift decision-making processes provide an open platform for your career progression.

title: Staff Robotic Sales Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
About the Role at RobCo

RobCo is building the category of Autonomous Industrial Robotics and we're doing it fast. We believe that automating the ordinary frees humans to do the extraordinary, and we're building the end-to-end robotics infrastructure to make that possible - hardware, software, and AI in one stack that just works.

 

As our Staff Robotic Sales Engineer (m/f/d), you are RobCo's most senior technical voice in sales, owning your own deals alongside Account Executives while setting the technical standards that make the whole Robotics Sales Engineering team stronger. If something is broken, you fix it. If something can be automated, you build it.

This is a technical leadership role without people management. You keep a quota with your own Account Executives, and a fixed part of your time goes into raising the technical bar across the team. You work where modular robotics, software and AI come together, and you help bring physical AI from the lab into real production. Sales leadership turns to you first when they want to know how strong the pipeline really is.

Your Responsibilities

  • Define how the team judges feasibility, including real-world limits beyond data sheets, edge cases and clear no-go criteria

  • Develop our requirement workshop format and handover standards further

  • Step into complex or escalating deals across the team, set the technical direction and stay involved until the responsible RSE can carry the case forward

  • Make the go/no-go call on difficult feasibility cases, review concepts before handover and approve larger price indications

  • Build reusable assets such as calculation models, reference layouts per use case and enablement material for Sales and our partners

  • Track which use cases keep coming up and which we win or lose, and feed these insights into focus areas and the product roadmap

  • Shape onboarding and ramp-up for new RSEs and give technical feedback across the team

  • Pitch to strategic customers, give talks at trade fairs and events, and decide with Marketing and Product what we demo and why

  • Stay the technical lead for your own Account Executives and share their quota

We're looking for someone who has:

  • Extensive experience in technical pre-sales, application engineering or automation projects, including time at a senior level

  • Experience working against a quota and winning complex deals

  • A track record as the person colleagues turn to when a feasibility question gets hard

  • The ability to recognize patterns across projects and turn them into rules, templates and tools that others use

  • Experience leading through expertise, with the trust of engineers and sales leaders in your technical judgement

  • The confidence to make a go/no-go call and stand behind it, even when a deal is on the line

  • Strong presence on stage and in the boardroom, from trade fair talks to pitches to strategic customers

  • Fluent German (C1+) and fluent English (C1+), and willingness to travel, around 30% of the time

  • Experience in physical AI (AI-based perception, learning-based manipulation, autonomous robots) is a plus

  • Experience building sales or partner enablement programs is a plus

  • A background at a robot manufacturer or system integrator is a plus

How you'll make an impact

  • You drive important, ambiguous initiatives to outcomes and define standards and approaches your peers adopt.

  • You translate strategy into execution with significant latitude and design improvements aligned with business goals.

  • You are a recognized subject matter expert at RobCo and set the technical or functional standards in your area.

Why join RobCo?

  • Develop modular, software-defined robotics solutions with us that set new standards in automation.

  • Help us build robots equipped with state-of-the-art AI that perceive their environment, analyze data, and make intelligent decisions in real time.

  • As part of a very dynamic and fast-growing scale-up, you will take on responsibility from day one, drive your own projects, and see the direct impact of your work.

  • Flat hierarchies, open communication, and regular 360° feedback enable fast decisions and support your professional and personal development.

  • Wellpass membership (7,200+ studios across Germany), regular team events, and a team that takes both the work and the culture seriously.

  • Flexible working hours, a modern office, and - depending on the role - the option to work from home.

  • Regular team events - from relaxed beer & pizza nights on the rooftop terrace to shared experiences on ski trips or at Oktoberfest.

About RobCo

Founded in Munich in 2020, RobCo leads the transition toward fully Autonomous Industrial Robotics. Our mission is to deploy RobCo in every factory - solving the industrial labor shortage through end-to-end robotics that just works. Powered by Physical AI, our solutions combine a scalable modular hardware architecture with intelligent software that continuously learns and improves, requiring zero upfront investment through our Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model.

We solve our customers' most pressing pain points - labor shortage, cost pressure, workplace safety, and national reshoring - across the full spectrum of Autonomous Industrial Robotics. In October 2026, RobCo reached unicorn status with a valuation exceeding one billion US dollars, with its valuation doubling in less than nine months. With $200M raised from investors including Sequoia, Lightspeed, Lingotto, Kindred, Cherry Ventures, and the European Tech Collective, 225+ people globally, and 3.5M+ operating hours in the field, we are deploying robots in factories across Europe and the United States - with our US operations headquartered in Austin, TX, and our Bay Area Lab in San Francisco.

Don’t meet every single requirement? If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

At RobCo, applicants are selected regardless of ethnic origin, religion, gender, age, disability, or sexual orientation. All decisions throughout the recruitment process are based solely on applicants’ qualifications, skills, knowledge, and experience, as well as relevant business requirements.

title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer - Moonpay Enterprise
description:
MoonPay Enterprise is for builders with something to prove.

This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend.

MoonPay Enterprise is the fund layer built for businesses. We power how stablecoins move through real financial operations: enterprises, fintechs, PSPs, wallets, and marketplaces running their treasuries, their cross-border flows, and their stablecoin operations on us. The goal is to make moving real money at scale as predictable as any other piece of financial infrastructure, with the compliance and controls CFOs need to say yes.

AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters.

You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together.

The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building the rails that businesses run real money on, for humans and agents. MoonPay ranked #2 in Crypto Services on Fortune's inaugural Crypto 100, made Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers 2026 (Top 25 in Finance), and landed on The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running.


The role

We’re hiring backend engineers across several openings within MoonPay Enterprise. All roles share the same foundation of designing and operating reliable, secure, high-throughput backend services, but each opening has a distinct focus. When you apply, tell us which track (or tracks) excites you most.

Track 1: KYB / KYC & Compliance Platform

Build the systems that let enterprises onboard safely and stay compliant across dozens of jurisdictions. You’ll own services powering business (KYB) and individual (KYC) verification flows, risk scoring, sanctions and AML screening, case management, and integrations with identity and compliance vendors. The challenge is making rigorous compliance feel invisible: fast, automated, and globally scalable, without ever compromising on regulatory obligations.

Track 2: New Product Lines, starting with Custody

Join us at the ground floor of new enterprise products, beginning with Custody. You’ll design the backend for secure digital asset storage and management for institutional clients: key management workflows, policy engines, transaction authorization, ledger integrity, and audit trails. This track suits engineers who love ambiguity, greenfield architecture, and building products from zero to one with enterprise-grade security requirements.

Track 3: Blockchain, Stablecoin Issuance & On-Chain Infrastructure

Work directly with blockchain protocols to power our stablecoin issuance business and on-chain products. You’ll build and operate services for minting, burning, and managing fully reserved stablecoins across chains, develop smart contract integrations on EVM chains and Solana, and design the indexing, monitoring, and reconciliation systems that keep on-chain and off-chain state in sync. Prior Solana (Rust) or Solidity development experience is a strong plus here.

Across all tracks, experience with fiat rails, banking integrations, or payments systems is very welcome. Much of our hardest work happens where traditional finance and crypto overlap.

What you’ll do

  • Design, build, and operate backend services written in Rust that process high volumes of financial transactions with strong guarantees around correctness, idempotency, and auditability
  • Own features end to end, from shaping the product spec through technical design, implementation, testing, deployment, and production monitoring. You won’t just receive work from product: as a domain expert, you’ll help define what we build and propose the work you consider most useful
  • Integrate with external partners such as banks, payment processors, blockchains, and identity and compliance vendors, and build the abstractions that make those integrations reliable
  • Improve engineering quality across observability, incident response, security practices, and API design
  • Collaborate closely with product, compliance, and other engineering teams across MoonPay’s global network
  • (Staff level) Set technical direction for your area, mentor other engineers, and drive architectural decisions that span multiple teams

About you

  • 5+ years of backend engineering experience (8+ for Staff), with a track record of shipping and operating production systems at scale
  • Strong backend experience with a statically compiled language (e.g. Rust, Go, C#, C++) is a must. Deep fundamentals matter more to us than your specific language history
  • Prior professional Rust experience is not required, but interest in Rust and motivation to become an expert in it are very welcome, since our services are written in Rust
  • Solid fundamentals in distributed systems, API design, data modeling, and asynchronous processing
  • Comfort working in domains where precision matters, such as financial systems, double-entry ledgers, reconciliation, or similarly correctness-critical software

title: Senior Commercial Manager
description:
ÜBER UNSERE COMPANY

freiheit.com wurde 1999 in Hamburg gegründet und entwickelt seitdem custom large-scale Softwareprodukte. Unsere Mission ist: “Ship great software”.

In mehr als zwei Jahrzehnten haben wir immer das ausgeliefert, was wir versprochen haben – “always on time, on budget, on target and on quality”.

85% unserer Members sind Software Engineers mit Abschlüssen in Informatik, Physik oder Mathematik, viele auch mit fundierten Kenntnissen in Maschinellem Lernen und Künstlicher Intelligenz. 

Seit über einem Vierteljahrhundert arbeiten wir für das „Who’s Who“ der deutschen und europäischen Industrie- und Handelsunternehmen.
Retail, Automotive, E-Commerce, Healthcare und mehr.

Unsere large-scale Softwareprodukte werden täglich von Millionen von Benutzern verwendet und sind entscheidend für den wirtschaftlichen Erfolg unserer Kunden. Jedes Produkt ist somit geschäftskritisch und ist von strategischer Relevanz. 

Gemeinsam machen wir “mission impossible possible”. 

Unser Team besteht aus 300+ Members aus der ganzen Welt. In unseren Büros in Hamburg und Lissabon bauen wir gemeinsam Produkte, die noch nie jemand zuvor entwickelt hat.

Unsere Teams arbeiten datengetrieben, um ihre eigene Produktivität ständig zu optimieren. Jedes Teammitglied übernimmt die “end-to-end” Verantwortung für seine Arbeit. Um erfolgreich zu sein, muss man produktiv sein. Um produktiv zu sein, muss man effizient und effektiv sein.

Technology never rests. Neither do we.



ÜBER DEINEN JOB

  • Zusammen mit unserem CEO übernimmst du Verantwortung für die erfolgreiche Geschäftsentwicklung bei freiheit.com 
  • Dafür hast du immer ein klares Ziel im Blick: Den Erfolg Deiner Kunden.
  • Enge Kundenbeziehungen sind für uns selbstverständlich, als verlässlicher Partner bist du öfters beim Kunden vor Ort und identifizierst mit ihm zusammen seine wichtigen strategischen Ziele.
  • Du bist strategischer Berater der Geschäftsführung und pflegst interne und externe Beziehungen.
    • Client Success
  • Deine Verantwortung ist die kaufmännische Projektsteuerung und die erfolgreiche Projektumsetzung, immer zusammen mit unseren Engineering Teams.
  • Mit Start und Ausbau eines Projektes stellst Du gemeinsam mit den Engineering Directors das für das Projekt optimale Engineering Team auf. 
  • Du arbeitest eng mit unseren Engineering Teams zusammen und identifizierst evtl. Frictions in dem jeweiligen Projekt. Deine Verantwortung ist es, diese zu beseitigen und damit sicherzustellen, dass das Engineering Team effektiv und effizient arbeiten kann und unsere “Optimal Work Environment” sichergestellt ist.
  • Du bist der Projektmanager und initiierst und moderierst regelmäßige Meetings, Review Sessions, Steering Committees.
    • Client Development
  • Zusätzlich entwickelst du Business und konvertierst unsere Leads zu Bestandskunden.
  • Du pflegst und erweiterst kontinuierlich Dein Netzwerk, verstehst die Potenziale bei unseren Kunden und fokussierst Dich zusammen mit dem Engineering aktiv auf den Kundenausbau.


    • ÜBER DICH

  • Du hast 5-6 Jahre Arbeitserfahrung in einem anspruchsvollen Umfeld (Konzern, Top-Tier Beratung oder Ähnliches).
  • Du hast einen erstklassigen Hochschulabschluss im Bereich der Wirtschaftswissenschaften, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen oder Ähnlichem.
  • Du bist im Herzen Unternehmer und hast ein ausgeprägtes “Customer-First Mindset” und ein erstklassiges Gespür im Umgang mit Kunden. 
  • Idealerweise hast Du Erfahrung bei der kommerziellen Planung und Auslieferung von komplexen large-scale Software-Projekten.
  • Du bist begeistert von Technologie und erstklassigem Software Engineering. 
  • Du arbeitest sehr präzise und bist sicher im Umgang mit Zahlen. 
  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch (mind. C1) und verhandlungssicheres Englisch. 
  • Du fühlst Dich wohl im Umgang mit Engineers & Non-Engineers, bist offen und ehrlich und arbeitest gern im Team. 
  • Du hast Durchhaltevermögen und “Situational Awareness” mit absolutem Willen zum Erfolg.
  • Du hast Spaß daran, selbständig zu arbeiten, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und an neuen Herausforderungen zu wachsen.
  • Du möchtest Dich kontinuierlich in allen kaufmännischen Themen weiterentwickeln, insbesondere das Thema Leadership interessiert Dich, um aufgrund unserer ambitionierten Wachstumspläne zukünftig Teamverantwortung zu übernehmen.

    • ÜBER UNSERE COMMUNITY

    Auf die Frage, warum jemand hier arbeitet, lautet die Antwort oft: „wegen der Menschen“ und „weil ich in meinem Leben noch nie so viel gelernt habe“.

    Wir glauben, dass produktive Menschen glückliche Menschen sind. 

    In unseren Engineering Hubs in Hamburg und Lissabon triffst du auf Menschen aus der ganzen Welt. 

    Hier hast du die Möglichkeit, mit intelligenten Menschen an spannenden Aufgaben zu arbeiten und Projekte von der Idee bis zur Auslieferung umzusetzen – end-to-end. 

    Ein wahrer Experte in seinem Fachgebiet wird man nicht über Nacht – dazu braucht es Jahre harter Arbeit und kontinuierliches Lernen. Als ein Member unserer Community wird viel von dir verlangt, und niemand kann die Arbeit für dich übernehmen.

    Unser Unternehmen ist ein Ort, an dem du die beste Version deiner selbst werden kannst. 

    ***Wir bieten keine reinen Remote-Stellen an. Wir arbeiten fünf Tage pro Woche im Büro. 

    DAZUGEHÖREN?

    Dann schicke uns Deine vollständigen Bewerbungsunterlagen (Lebenslauf und Zeugnisse) über unser Bewerberportal. Und bei Fragen zu Deiner Bewerbung oder dem Bewerbungsprozess steht Dir Bianca Mioc unter +49 40/890584-0 persönlich zur Verfügung.

title: Buyer Development Sr Director DACH
description:
Company at a Glance
OpenX is focused on unleashing the full economic potential of digital media companies. We do this by making digital advertising markets and technologies that are designed to deliver optimal value to publishers and advertisers on every ad served across all screens.

At OpenX, we have built a team that is uniquely experienced in designing and operating high-scale ad marketplaces, and we are constantly on the lookout for thoughtful, creative executors who are as fascinated as we are about finding new ways to apply a blend of market design, technical innovation, operational excellence, and empathetic partner service to the frontiers of digital advertising.

OpenX is looking for a senior, commercially driven Buyer Development leader to establish and grow our demand-side business across DACH.
This is the first dedicated Buyer Development role in-market. The role will be directly responsible for generating revenue across agencies, holdcos, and clients / brands, building senior relationships and commercial foundations required for long-term growth.

The successful candidate will open senior buyer relationships, build and manage pipeline, progress strategic opportunities, and convert demand-side engagement into measurable revenue outcomes.

This is a senior individual contributor role to begin with. As the DACH opportunity matures, the ambition is for this person to help build and potentially lead a broader regional Buyer Development function once clear market proof points have been established.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Own Revenue Growth

  • Take direct responsibility for generating and growing buyer-led revenue across agencies, holdcos, and clients / brands in DACH.

     

  • Build and manage a qualified pipeline across PMP, curation, SPO, CTV, data-led activation, OpenX Select, premium supply, AI-led solutions, and direct buyer partnerships.

     

  • Convert senior relationships into commercial outcomes through consultative selling, strategic account planning, business cases, QBRs, joint business plans, and deal progression.

  • Maintain strong commercial discipline around pipeline, forecasting, revenue progression, and opportunity prioritisation.

     

  • Build the Market
  • Establish OpenX’s Buyer Development presence in DACH as the first dedicated in-market hire.
  • Create a clear map of priority buyers, agencies, holdcos, brands, DSPs, data partners, senior decision-makers, trading models, and commercial pathways.
  • Identify where OpenX can create the most meaningful and scalable impact in the region.
  • Build the foundations for a future regional team, including account prioritisation, pipeline discipline, market feedback loops, and cross-functional ways of working.
  • Work Cross-Functionally
  • Work closely with Sales, Account Management, Product, Marketing, global Buyer Development, DSP Strategic Partnerships, and the Data Partner function to shape, activate, measure, and scale DACH opportunities.
  • Partner with DSP Strategic Partnerships to improve buyer access, support SPO conversations, and ensure agency and client demand can be activated efficiently through priority DSP routes.
  • Partner with the Data Partner function to identify relevant data-led opportunities for DACH buyers, including curated marketplaces, audience-led activation, and strategic client solutions.
  • Build OpenX’s Market Presence
  • Represent OpenX as a credible senior voice in the DACH programmatic market.
  • Support OpenX’s visibility through senior meetings, client education, industry events, roundtables, and thought leadership.
  • Position OpenX around key buyer priorities including transparency, sustainability, premium supply, curation, data quality, supply path optimisation, and a healthier digital advertising ecosystem.

    • Requirements:
  • 7+ years of experience as a senior commercial individual contributor with deep knowledge of the DACH programmatic advertising ecosystem and a strong network across agencies, holdcos, brands, DSPs, and strategic partners.
  • The ideal candidate will have a proven track record of revenue ownership, opening senior relationships, building pipeline, and converting strategic opportunities into commercial outcomes.
  • They should be credible with senior clients and partners, highly self-motivated, commercially disciplined, and comfortable building a market from an early-stage position.
  • Fluency in German and English is required.

    We take responsible risks and own and learn from our mistakes. We recognize and repeat success. We actively seek out and provide constructive feedback. We adapt quickly and embrace change. We tackle growth and learning with real urgency. We are endlessly curious.

title: Build Your Own Internship – m/f/d (min. 6 Months)
description:
Help Us Change the Way the World Works

 

Build something that matters.

Langdock exists to change the way the world works, bridging the gap between what technology can do and what people actually do with it. We bring all leading AI models into one secure, model-agnostic platform and make them usable across entire organizations. Over 10,000 companies use our platform every day, from fast-growing startups to some of Europe’s largest enterprises. Their employees open Langdock to draft strategies, analyze documents, or automate workflows, helping them to work smarter, think more creatively, and reach their full potential.

 

About the Role

This is a full-time internship of at least 6 months at our Berlin HQ, and it is not a regular internship application. We don’t want your CV first. We want to see what you have built.

If you build with AI because you can’t stop, with Langdock, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or anything else, show us. If your project convinces us, we shape the internship around you and your strengths.

 

What We Want to See

Record a Loom of something you built with AI. It should be no longer than 5 minutes. Two kinds of projects get our attention:

  • Something that would help Langdock. Look at our product roadmap and at our product, and build something that solves a real problem for us or our customers. That could be a feature prototype, an internal tool, a GTM engine, a support automation, an eval setup, or something we haven’t thought of yet.

  • A genuine passion project. Something you built because you couldn’t stop thinking about it, and that shows how you think.

What we don’t want: basic chatbots, simple prompt wrappers, “summarize my inbox” agents, or linear three-step workflows. Our customers build those every day. Show us something that made you think hard, and that makes us think too.

 

What Your Loom Should Cover

  • The problem: what you solved and why it matters.

  • The demo: show it working live, not on slides.

  • How it’s built: the models, tools, architecture, and key decisions behind it.

  • What broke: where it failed and what you learned from that.

  • What’s next: what you would build at Langdock if you joined.

 

What You Will Do

  • Own a real project. Ideally it’s the one you showed us. You take it from prototype to something our team or customers actually use.

  • Work directly with the team. You work alongside Product, Engineering, or GTM, depending on where your project lives.

  • Ship, measure, iterate. You present your progress regularly and decide based on real feedback.

The Role

Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As Compliance Director and AML at Doit Lithuania, you will build and run our compliance and anti-money-laundering function from day one.

You will act as our Compliance Officer and AML Officer, and report directly to the management board. You will be independent of the business lines you monitor. You will run compliance and AML for a digital investment platform serving clients in Lithuania and across the European Economic Area.

What You’ll Own

  • Write and own the compliance and AML/CTF policies and procedures.

  • Build the business-wide AML risk assessment, customer risk scoring and risk appetite.

  • Design remote onboarding controls with our KYC partners, including enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk clients.

  • Design and tune transaction monitoring scenarios for brokerage activity.

  • Run sanctions screening at onboarding, on an ongoing basis and on payments.

  • File suspicious activity reports with the FNTT and suspicious order reports under MAR.

  • Run the compliance monitoring programme and report to the board.

  • Approve marketing communications and oversee product governance, complaints and conflicts of interest.

  • Manage the regulatory relationship with the Bank of Lithuania on compliance and AML matters.

  • Prepare the firm for the EU AML Regulation, which applies from July 2027.

  • Build the compliance and AML team as the business grows.

What We’re Looking For

  • Significant experience in AML/CTF at a regulated EU financial institution. Ideally at an investment firm, neobroker, neobank or e-money institution.

  • Experience with digital onboarding and remote identity verification at scale.

  • Hands-on experience building risk assessments, monitoring scenarios and EDD processes.

  • Experience filing suspicious activity reports and handling regulatory inspections.

  • Knowledge of MiFID II conduct and investment-services compliance, or the ability to learn it fast.

  • Experience selecting and overseeing KYC, screening and monitoring tools.

  • Strong judgment and the confidence to challenge senior colleagues.

  • Clear, concise writing for policies, board reports and regulators.

  • A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a key function holder.

  • Based in Lithuania, or open to relocating to Lithuania.

Nice to Have

  • Lithuanian language ability.

  • An existing working relationship with the Bank of Lithuania or the FNTT.

  • Knowledge of Lithuanian AML law and Bank of Lithuania instructions.

  • Experience with clients across several EEA countries.

  • CAMS (ACAMS) or ICA certification.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only want to attend meetings.

  • Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.

  • People who copy policies from templates without fitting them to the business.

  • People who say no without offering a compliant way forward.

  • People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions.

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

You must be a European citizen or already hold a valid right to work in Lithuania. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

description:
Bei Knuspr definieren wir den Lebensmitteleinkauf neu. Um täglich Tausende Kunden zuverlässig mit frischen, regionalen Lebensmitteln und Artikeln des täglichen Bedarfs zu beliefern, braucht es ein hocheffizientes operatives Rückgrat.

Als Central Flow Lead bist du die zentrale Steuerungsinstanz für den Personaleinsatz und den operativen Durchfluss in unseren deutschen Fulfillment Centern. Von deinem Büroarbeitsplatz in Garching überwachst du die operative Leistung in Echtzeit, steuerst die Personalkapazitäten dynamisch und stimmst dich direkt mit den Teams vor Ort ab, um jeden Standort auf maximaler Effizienz zu halten.

Deine Mission ist direkt: Live-Daten in unmittelbare Handlungen übersetzen. Indem du Engpässe frühzeitig erkennst, Personal bedarfsgerecht zwischen den Bereichen ausbalancierst und die Abläufe synchronisierst, stellst du sicher, dass jede Bestellung reibungslos bearbeitet und pünktlich ausgeliefert wird.

Warum diese Rolle spannend ist:

  • Büroarbeitsplatz: Du arbeitest ausschließlich im Control Office in Garching, ohne körperliche Lagertätigkeit, und steuerst die Abläufe vom Schreibtisch aus über Dashboards und Steuerungstools

  • Einfluss auf nationaler Ebene: Steuere die Personaleinsatzplanung und den operativen Durchsatz mehrerer deutscher Fulfillment Center

  • Echtzeit-Entscheidungen: Arbeite in einem hochdynamischen Umfeld, in dem Live-Daten unmittelbar zu spürbaren operativen Anpassungen führen

  • Intelligente Logistik & Technologie: Gestalte die Schnittstelle zwischen Lagerautomatisierung, WMS-Plattformen und datengestützter Personalsteuerung aktiv mit

Was wir zusätzlich zum Grundgehalt bieten:

  • Tägliche Essenspauschale: Zusätzliche 9,00 € steuerfreier Essenszuschuss pro Arbeitstag

  • Täglicher Fahrtkostenzuschuss: Zusätzliche 5,00 € täglicher Zuschuss zu deinen Fahrtkosten

  • Halbjährliche Gutscheine: 300,00 € in Gutscheinen zweimal jährlich (insgesamt 600,00 € pro Jahr)

  • Knuspr Xtra Account: 10 % Cashback auf deine Bestellungen direkt als Knuspr-Guthaben

  • CorporateBenefits: Vergünstigungen auf Fitness, Reisen, Event-Tickets, Shopping und mehr

Deine Aufgaben

  • Abläufe im Blick behalten: Du verfolgst unsere Dashboards in Echtzeit und sorgst dafür, dass die richtigen Kollegen/-innen zur richtigen Zeit im richtigen Bereich sind. Dafür nutzt du unsere zentralen Steuerungstools

  • Kapazitäten flexibel ausbalancieren: Wenn sich das Auftragsvolumen oder die Prioritäten an einem Standort ändern, passt du Personalverteilung und Schichtpläne entsprechend an

  • Operative Kennzahlen aktiv steuern: Du hast kritische Bereitstellungszeiten und Leerläufe fest im Blick, deckst Engpässe sofort auf und greifst korrigierend ein

  • Standortübergreifend zusammenarbeiten: Du stimmst dich eng mit den Führungskräften und Teams auf der Fläche ab, damit Anpassungen gut umgesetzt werden und unsere Prozessstandards eingehalten werden

  • Gemeinsam besser werden: Du analysierst Schichtleistungen, entdeckst wiederkehrende Prozesslücken, überprüfst gemeinsam mit den Standorten unsere SOP-Standards und hilfst mit deinem Feedback, unsere internen Tools weiterzuentwickeln

  • Operativer Hintergrund: Eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung als Speditionskaufmann/-frau oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation, wie z.B. praktische Erfahrung als Disponent, in der Schichtkoordination, operativen Einsatzplanung oder Personaleinsatzsteuerung, idealerweise in Logistik, Lager, Einzelhandel, E-Commerce oder Fulfillment.

  • Erfahrung in einem Leitstand, Control Center oder Control Tower, im Workforce Management oder mit automatisierten Lägern ist ein Plus.

  • Sprachkenntnisse: Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse für die tägliche Kommunikation. Gute Ungarischkenntnisse für die klare Abstimmung mit den Teams auf der Fläche sind ein großer Vorteil

  • Schichtbereitschaft: Bereitschaft zur Arbeit in einem 24-Stunden-Dreischichtsystem von Montag bis Samstag

description:
TEAMWFP ist eine Agentur für kreatives VkF-Marketing in Mönchengladbach. Seit 45 Jahren betreut die Agentur Unternehmen aus Handel und Finanzen in der Verkaufs- und Markenkommunikation: Prospekte, Mailings, Instore Design, Verpackungen und Kampagnen, für Kunden wie PENNY, Kaufland oder die Sparkassen. Gesucht wird eine erfahrene Beraterin oder ein erfahrener Berater als Senior Projektmanager Marketing (m/w/d) in Vollzeit: die Schnittstelle zwischen Kreation und Kunde, mit eigenen Kunden und einem Beraterteam von fünf bis sechs Leuten.

Das Besondere bei TEAMWFP: Jeder Kunde wird auf Senior-Level betreut. Es gibt keinen Kunden, der an Praktikanten und Junioren abgegeben wird, und keine Ebene, die zwischen dir und deiner Arbeit steht. Im Agenturverbund arbeiten rund 30 Leute. Große Meetings gibt es kaum, vieles wird kurz über den Flur abgestimmt, und die beiden Creative Directors arbeiten selbst mit am Produkt. Du berätst viele Kunden aus Handel und Finanzen, ohne mehrere Ebenen zwischen dir und den Entscheidungen und ohne jeden Tag nach Düsseldorf zu pendeln.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du bist die Schnittstelle zwischen Kreation und Kunde und koordinierst jedes Projekt vom Briefing bis zur Produktionsreife.
  • Du vertrittst die Agentur in Abstimmungen beim Kunden und arbeitest dich inhaltlich in alle Projekte ein.
  • Du bereitest Briefings verständlich für dein Team auf und erarbeitest kommunikative Lösungen, allein oder mit der Kreation.
  • Du prüfst alle Werbemittel formal und inhaltlich, bevor sie an den Kunden gehen, und kalkulierst und überwachst die Kosten selbst.
  • Du übernimmst Beratungsaufgaben der Geschäftsführung und steuerst das Beraterteam mit.

Was du mitbringst

  • Eine Ausbildung als Kaufmann oder Kauffrau für Marketingkommunikation oder ein Studium im Bereich Marketing. Erfahrung zählt mehr als der Abschluss.
  • Erfahrung im Agenturumfeld oder in einer Marketingabteilung auf Kundenseite, Handelsmarketing ist ein Plus.
  • Fundiertes Marketingwissen, mit dem du Kunden strategisch berätst und Leistungen verkaufst.
  • Du greifst gern zum Hörer, behältst in vollen Phasen die Ruhe und bist sicher in Excel, Word und PowerPoint. Sehr gutes Deutsch ist Voraussetzung.

Was dich bei TEAMWFP erwartet

  • Ein Gehalt ab 4.000 € im Monat, je nach Erfahrung nach oben offen.
  • Senior-Level auf jedem Kunden: In Beratung und Kreation sitzen erfahrene Leute am Tisch, Entscheidungen fallen schnell und direkt.
  • Viele Kunden und nie dasselbe: Vom Handel bis zur Bank übernimmt die Agentur fast jede Aufgabe, die ein Kunde stellt, und arbeitet bei den meisten Kunden nicht in festen Teams.
  • Gleitzeit mit Kernzeit von 10 bis 15 Uhr, Überstunden werden ausgeglichen. Wochenend- und Nachtschichten gibt es nicht.
  • Ein fester, eigener Arbeitsplatz in kleinen Büros für eine bis drei Personen statt Großraum und Desk Sharing.
  • Ein Backsteinbau im Nordpark mit Aufenthaltsraum und Billardtisch, aus Gladbach auch gut mit dem Fahrrad erreichbar.

Ehrlich gesagt: Als Schnittstelle hängst du an vielen Leuten. Vom Kunden brauchst du Infos, von Konzept und Gestaltung pünktliche Ergebnisse, und phasenweise wird es stressig. Der Tipp aus dem Team: von Anfang an die eigenen Grenzen setzen.

Diese Stelle wird über JobMatches vorgestellt. Bewirb dich jetzt als Senior Projektmanager Marketing (m/w/d) bei TEAMWFP in Mönchengladbach. Nach einem kurzen Telefonat lernst du Kim Finocchiaro und die Geschäftsführung persönlich kennen.

  • Deep familiarity with legal technology and AI tools, with an ability to quickly develop and demonstrate platform expertise

title: (Senior) Electronics Engineer, Hardware & Firmware (f/m/d)
description:
About TACTILIA

At TACTILIA, we are building the industry-ready robotic hand that closes one of the biggest gaps in Physical AI. Spun out of Schunk, the global market leader in gripping technology, we combine a decade of robotic-hand expertise and real industrial access with the speed and ambition of a deep-tech startup.

This isn't a research project waiting for its first customer. We already have a product, customers are ready to use it, and we are launching now. Your work will directly shape the electronics, actuators, and embedded systems that make that possible.

You will join at the moment when the hard engineering questions become real product decisions: how do we make a highly capable robotic hand reliable, manufacturable, serviceable, and simple enough to deploy on a real shop floor?

The Role

As an Electronics Engineer (Embedded Hardware & Firmware) at TACTILIA Robotics, you will help design and build the physical and low-level intelligence that brings our robotic hands to life.

You will own the complete embedded hardware and firmware stack—from schematics and high-density multilayer layouts to the real-time C/C++ firmware running directly on the metal.

Fitting multiple drives, high-density tactile arrays, and power electronics into a hand-sized volume means every decision is a tight balance of space, thermals, signal integrity, and manufacturability. You will work closely with the CTO and cross-functional team, moving smoothly between architecture, circuit design, and the lab to solve complex problems where physics meets code.

What you will do:

  • Own the hardware architecture. Design schematics and high-density, multilayer PCB layouts (mixed-signal, tight thermal/EMC constraints) built for modularity across product variants—not a one-off prototype.

  • Build control hardware and firmware that can't miss a beat. Search, evaluate, test, and integrate actuator hardware alongside motor drivers for compact servo drives; write deterministic real-time firmware (C/C++) for control loops, timing-critical execution, limit monitoring, and fault handling.

  • Choose the right sensor and make the data mean something. Search, evaluate, test, and integrate sensor hardware for tactile sensing and proprioception (position and force); design low-noise readout electronics, signal conditioning, filtering, and calibration pipelines to deliver clean, low-latency telemetry to the software stack.

  • Ship rock-solid bootloaders and drivers. Build field-updatable bootloaders, low-level drivers, and secure, fail-safe update strategies across product generations—documented and reliable, not tribal knowledge.

  • Build interfaces customers actually want to integrate. Implement and maintain fieldbus and hardware communication layers (EtherCAT, CANopen, Ethernet) aligned cleanly with higher-level software and robot controllers.

  • Debug on real hardware. Own the lab bring-up process from first power-on to full validation. Trace issues across the hardware, firmware, and mechanical boundaries with scopes, logic analyzers, and thermal imaging.

  • Build security into the product from day one. Support Cyber Resilience Act compliance by integrating secure boot, signed firmware updates, and hardware-level trust mechanisms early in the design cycle.

  • Build for series production, not just the lab. Design for manufacturing and test (DFM/DFT), select resilient supply-chain components with second sources, run EMC pre-compliance, and drive hardware through production ramp-up.

  • Work across the whole team. Tight loop with Mechanics, Software, and System Applications—translating mechanical and control requirements into robust, deployable electronics.

What you bring:

  • A degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field.

  • 5–10 years of experience developing embedded hardware and firmware for mechatronic products, including at least one product taken into series production.

  • Proven expertise in schematic capture and multilayer PCB layout (Altium, KiCad, or similar), specifically for space-constrained, mixed-signal designs.

  • Strong C/C++ skills on bare-metal or RTOS (ARM Cortex-M or similar) with a deep understanding of timing, concurrency, memory, and register-level hardware control.

  • Hands-on experience with BLDC/DC motor driver design, current/velocity/position control loops, and low-level sensor interfacing.

  • A strong hardware mindset: you enjoy lab bring-up, signal-integrity debugging, and getting to the bottom of transient issues with a scope or logic analyzer.

  • Fluent English; German is a plus, not a requirement.

Bonus:

  • Miniature electronics, high-density PCB packaging, or tight thermal constraints

  • Tactile, force/torque, or contact-rich sensor arrays

  • Real-time fieldbuses (EtherCAT, CANopen)

  • Product security: secure boot, signed firmware, CRA, IEC 62443

  • Functional safety standards (Machinery Regulation, ISO/TS 15066)

The next chapter of robotics won't be built in a lab. It will be built by people who care about what happens when technology meets the real world.

At TACTILIA, you'll work on one of the hardest open problems in robotics: giving machines the dexterity, reliability, and robustness they need to interact with the physical world at industrial scale.

title: Talent & People Lead (m/f/d)
description:
About VIA HealthTech

VIA turns a therapy session into a finished session note, and session notes into a complete psychological report. That is work which used to cost therapists hours every week.

We are the market leading AI assistant for psychotherapists. Over 4,000 psychotherapists across the DACH region use VIA every day, and we process hundreds of thousands of sessions per month. We are ISO 27001:2022 certified and hold a BSI C5 attestation.

We are a multidisciplinary team of 12 in Berlin-Mitte. Being the market leader in AI documentation is our starting position, not our goal. We are going much deeper, into the therapeutic process itself and into how a practice is run, with products that will be regulated as medical devices under EU MDR.

The role

We are 12 today and plan to roughly double in the next year, across engineering, our clinical team and go-to-market. We are bootstrapped. Every salary is paid from revenue, not from a funding round, and a wrong hire costs us a year we cannot buy back. We cannot afford that mistake, so we do not hire good. We hire exceptional.

Today, hiring lands between three founder calendars that are already full, or with agencies. Both fill roles. Neither builds anything that stays. We would rather internalise it: one person who knows our bar, owns the whole pipeline and builds the people function around it. You are not joining an HR team. You are becoming it.

Recruiting is the core of this role, and the measure in year one is simple: every role we open, filled on time with someone excellent, closed by you. Everything else in HR is yours to build lean behind that.

What you'll own

  • The whole funnel, for every role. Briefing with the hiring founder, the job ad, sourcing, screening, interview loops, references, offer, close. You are the first conversation a candidate has with VIA, and the one who gets them over the line

  • Sourcing that does not wait for applications. The people we want are rarely looking. Outbound on LinkedIn and beyond, our network, the places where therapists, engineers and salespeople actually are. We use agencies today. After you, we do not

  • The bar. A process that reliably separates excellent from good: structured interviews, take-home challenges with the hiring team, scorecards, fast decisions. You say no to candidates the founders like, and you say it with reasons

  • Candidate experience. Answers within days, not weeks. Every candidate, hired or not, leaves with a better opinion of VIA than they came with

  • Onboarding. A new engineer ships on day two, a new Sales Manager runs their first demo in week one. You build the path from signed contract to productive, together with the hiring lead

  • A lean people function. Contracts, probation reviews, feedback and performance cycles, compensation bands and the tooling behind them. Founders' time out, structure in. Our ISO 27001 and C5 frameworks carry HR controls, from joiner and leaver processes to security training, and you own those with the Security & Compliance Lead (who may be one of your first hires)

  • The team as it doubles. Rituals, offsites, the things that keep a company twice this size feeling like the 12-person one that got here

Your profile

Must-have

  • A track record of closing hard roles yourself, in-house or at an agency, with numbers you can show: hires per year, time to hire, offer acceptance. Senior engineers and salespeople at minimum

  • Real sourcing craft. You find people who are not applying and get them to take the call

  • Judgement about people. You can tell exceptional from polished in a first conversation, and explain the difference

  • Closing instinct. You know what moves a candidate who holds three offers, and you negotiate for us without losing them

  • Builder mentality. Processes, templates and tooling you set up yourself, because there is nobody else to do it

  • Working knowledge of German employment basics: contracts, probation, notice periods and the thresholds that matter as we grow. Payroll and legal are outsourced; you know when to call them

  • Hunger. You want to build the people function of a company that is going to be much bigger, not run one that already exists

  • Fluent German and English. Our candidates and contracts are in German, parts of our team work in English

Strong plus

  • You have been the first People hire somewhere and built from zero

  • Employer branding, from the careers page to events

  • AI tools as a matter of course. One person using them well replaces a recruiting team

  • You have recruited in a regulated health-tech environment

This role is not for you if

  • You want to run HR and let someone else do the hiring. Hiring is the job

  • You need an ATS, an employer brand and inbound applicants already in place. You build those

  • You hire to fill a seat. We would rather leave it empty

What we offer

  • A team that outperforms. DACH market leader for AI assistance in psychotherapy within two years, bootstrapped, with a team of 12. Our plans from here are considerably bolder, and we hire people who want to be part of it

  • Ownership of a core function from day one. Every person who joins VIA in the next year came through you. There is no clearer measure of impact

  • High autonomy. Competence and execution are what count here. We do not put obstacles in your way

  • Direct work with the founders. Decisions in hours, not weeks, including on offers

  • Competitive salary plus equity, so that you participate in the company's success

  • Office in Berlin-Mitte with flexible hours, latest equipment and any tool you need. Berlin-based hybrid is our preference for this role

We are not looking for someone to administer HR. We are looking for the person who finds the people VIA's next year depends on, and then builds the function that keeps them.

Sounds like you? A short CV or your LinkedIn profile is enough. If there is a hire you are proud of, tell us about that one.

title: Director Service Accounts (m/f/d)
description:
Director Service Accounts @ Sereact 🦾

Director Service Accounts (m/f/d) · Stuttgart, with frequent travel to customer sites across Europe · Reports to the VP Operations · Full-time

Who we are

Sereact builds the robot brain for physical work. Cortex, our vision-language-action foundation model, is hardware-agnostic: the same model runs single-arm and dual-arm systems and mobile manipulators that pick, sort and handle returns in live production across Europe and the US. Customers include Zalando, IKEA, BMW, Rohlik and DHL.

Founded in 2021 in Stuttgart, with an R&D hub in Zurich and a US office in Boston. We have raised more than $145 million, most recently a Series B led by Headline, with Zalando as a strategic investor. We work in small, senior teams with a flat structure; execution counts more than titles.

Why this role, why now

The Site Acceptance Test is where a deployment ends and a customer’s operation begins. From that day our robots pick in someone else’s building, every shift, against targets the customer measures. Many of our customers buy Sereact as a service: they pay for robots that work, not for robots that were delivered.

Our deployments are growing from single robots to fleets, and the site that performs is the site that grows. We now want one leader who owns every live site from SAT on: keeps it at target, brings it everything we ship in software and hardware, speaks for the customer inside Sereact, and turns a working site into a growing one.

The Real-World Learning Loop runs through your sites

Cortex learns from live deployments. Every station at a customer is part of that loop, so a station that is down is more than a service problem: a cell sitting dark is a stopped sensor.

  • In-Situ Policy Execution. Every live station runs the current policy in a real operation. Your surface on it: each site at target, every shift.

  • Continuous Data Acquisition. Robots annotate their own work while they run. Your surface on it: stations that run and stay connected, so the data keeps coming.

  • Data Curation and Learning. Failures and edge cases decide what Cortex learns next. Your surface on it: what your sites tell us reaches engineering and research with the context they need.

  • Evaluation and Policy Redeployment. Updated policies pass validation gates before they return to the fleet. Your surface on it: they land in your customers’ operations on a schedule the customer can plan around, with a way back if something is off.

A site that runs well teaches Cortex more, and it grows.

Responsibilities

  • Take over every site at SAT. Set the standard for what a site needs before your team takes it on: documentation, open points, spare parts, contacts and targets. If a site is not ready, it stays with deployment until it is.

  • Keep every site at target. Own each site’s performance against its contract: availability, throughput and pick success. See a problem coming before the customer does, and run the recovery plan when a site falls behind.

  • Run planned change. Software releases and model updates reach customer operations in a rhythm customers can plan around: release notes, change windows, blackout periods, validation on site and a rollback path.

  • Run hardware updates and retrofits across the installed base, from new gripper generations to station upgrades and fixes, with Hardware Engineering and the field teams, without stopping the customer’s operation.

  • Get every site ready for peak: hypercare and coverage plans for the weeks that matter most to our customers, from Black Friday to the January returns wave.

  • Be the customer’s advocate inside Sereact. Bring their priorities into product, R&D, hardware and operations, make sure what we promised at SAT holds, and own the customer communication when something goes wrong.

  • Take each site from SAT to expansion with Strategic Accounts: the performance evidence, the site capacity and the technical plan for the next stations. Strategic Accounts own the contract; you make the expansion ready to happen.

  • Report site health customers trust: one view of every site, monthly performance reports and the operational part of every business review.

  • Build and lead the Service Accounts team: Service Account Managers who each own a portfolio of live sites, and a playbook that still works when the installed base is ten times larger.

  • Work hand in hand with Deployment, Technical Support & Field Service, Hardware Engineering, R&D and Strategic Accounts, so a live site gets one coordinated answer, not five.

Not in scope, by design

  • Deployment up to SAT stays with our deployment teams. You set the bar for what you take over.

  • Incidents, the support desk, field technicians and spare parts logistics stay with Technical Support & Field Service. You own the site; they own the ticket.

  • Contracts, pricing and the expansion deal itself stay with Strategic Accounts. You make the case; they sign it.

  • Product and hardware design stay with engineering. You bring them what the field needs.

What makes this role hard

  • Every change to a live operation is a risk, and not changing is a risk too: the fleet only gets better if updates reach it. You make both safe.

  • Our robots work in other people’s buildings: their WMS, their conveyors, their shift patterns, their peak. Much of what decides a site’s performance is not ours, and it is still your problem.

  • You sit between the customer and our teams. Sometimes the customer’s priority is not ours. You argue for it, or you explain honestly why not.

  • The installed base grows faster than any team. What works by heroics today breaks at ten times the size.

Your first 12 months

  • First 90 days: know every live site and its people; one named owner, one health view and a clear status against target for each; a handover standard at SAT agreed with deployment.

  • By month 6: releases and retrofits in a rhythm customers can plan around; peak season run on hypercare plans; account plans with Strategic Accounts for the largest customers; the first Service Account Managers hired.

  • By month 12: every site at target or on a dated recovery plan; expansions coming out of the installed base; a playbook ready to take to the US.

What you bring

  • 8+ years owning live installations of complex automation after go-live (warehouse automation, intralogistics, robotics or comparable 24/7 systems), as service account manager, technical account manager, customer success or service delivery lead, including at least three years leading a team.

  • You did it while the installed base grew from tens to hundreds of sites, and you built the processes rather than inheriting them.

  • Technical enough to read a log, follow a root cause and hold your own with engineers. Commercial enough to sit with a customer’s operations director and talk performance, cost and growth.

  • You have run releases, upgrades and retrofit programs in live operations without stopping them.

  • Customers trust you because you tell them early and you tell them straight.

  • Fluent English and German; another European language is a plus.

  • You are happy to spend a large part of your week at customer sites.
